title: Grêmio Aims for Copa do Brasil Semifinals Return
seoTitle: Grêmio Aims for Copa do Brasil Semifinals Return
subtitle: The Tricolor Faces Inter in the Quarterfinal Second Leg
excerpt: Grêmio, the second-most successful club in the Copa do Brasil, seeks to return to the semifinals after six years. The return leg against Internacional is scheduled for.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
Grêmio has the mission to return to the Copa do Brasil semifinals, after six years without being among the top four. The team, led by Luís Castro, faces Internacional in the quarterfinal second leg, scheduled for Thursday, September 3, at 8 PM, at Grêmio Arena.

The Challenge of the Quarterfinal Second Leg

The goalless draw in the first leg, held at Beira-Rio, left Grêmio in a delicate position. The return leg will be decisive in determining who advances to the semifinals.

Grêmio's History in the Copa do Brasil

The Tricolor is the second-most successful champion of the competition, with five titles. The last time they reached the semifinals was in 2020, when they faced São Paulo. The first leg ended 1-0 in favor of Grêmio, with a goal from Diego Souza, and the return leg ended 0-0. The club advanced to the final but ended up as runner-up to Palmeiras.

Relevant Statistics for the Tricolor

Grêmio has accumulated 15 semifinals played in the history of the Copa do Brasil. The team has already won the trophies in 1989, 1991, 1993, 1994, 1995, 1997, 2001, 2016, and 2020. Each title had a different coach leading the team: Cláudio Duarte (1989), Luiz Felipe Scolari (1994), Evaristo de Macedo (1997), Tite (2001), and Renato Portaluppi (2016).

  • Top Scorer: Striker Paulo Nunes leads with 15 goals in the tournament;
  • Goalkeeper: Danrlei holds the record for most matches defended for the Tricolor in the competition, with 58 games;
  • Achievements: 5 titles, 4 runner-up finishes, and over 340 goals scored in the history of the Copa do Brasil;
  • Undefeated Triumphs: The 1989 and 1994 trophies were won without losing any match;
  • Last Title: 2020, when Grêmio advanced to the final;
  • Last Semifinal: 2020, against São Paulo;
  • Last Decisive Match: 2020, at Morumbi, ended 0-0;
  • Last Victory: 2020, 1-0 at Grêmio Arena, with a goal from Diego Souza.

What's at Stake for Grêmio

If Grêmio wins the return leg against Internacional, they will advance to the Copa do Brasil semifinals. The match will be decisive, as the result will determine who reaches the final phase of the competition. The club seeks to leverage its players' experience and the coach's strategy to overcome their rival.

Grêmio's Current Scenario in the Brasileirão

Grêmio is on thin ice in the Brasileirão, which could affect their performance in the Copa do Brasil. The pressure for results in the championship might influence the team's preparation for the decisive match against Internacional.

Internacional and Grêmio's Challenge

Internacional, also facing difficulties in the Brasileirão, could pose a tough opponent for Grêmio. The return leg will be an opportunity for Grêmio to demonstrate their ability to overcome challenges and advance in the competition.

With information from GZH, R7 Esportes.
